citation: Lei et al. (2025), The water use of data center workloads: A review and assessment of key determinants
system_scope: Data-center workload water use; operational and electricity-related drivers
empirical_data_or_code: Publisher article; Berkeley Lab publication page
source_supported_finding: Reports workload-level water-use variation exceeding 10,000-fold and ranks server efficiency, grid water factors, utilization, cooling type, infrastructure efficiency, climate, inactive-server share, and refresh cycle among determinants.
relevance_to_this_project: Supports scenario factors and site-/workload-specific water accounting rather than a universal water-per-compute constant.
limitation_or_non_claim: Does not evaluate AI waste-heat recovery through membrane distillation or establish net water benefit for this project.
license_or_reuse_note: Reuse terms for article/full text must be checked at the source; DOI and metadata may be cited.

citation: Herrera et al. (2025), Sustainable AI infrastructure: A scenario-based forecast of water footprint under uncertainty
system_scope: Global AI data-center operational, electricity-related, and embodied water through 2050
empirical_data_or_code: Authors report data and code at https://github.com/manuelhf/waterforAI
source_supported_finding: Separates facility operational, off-site electricity, and embodied water; uses scenario-based probabilistic forecasting and sensitivity analysis.
relevance_to_this_project: Provides a precedent for uncertainty-aware AI-infrastructure water accounting and an open comparison source for assumptions.
limitation_or_non_claim: Global scenario forecast is not a site-specific causal model of recoverable heat, MD cooling constraints, or avoided freshwater consumption.
license_or_reuse_note: Publisher record identifies open access; source code/data repository terms must be checked independently.

citation: Malaguti et al. (2026), Waste heat won't make membrane distillation cool: Thermodynamic analysis of cooling and pumping burdens
system_scope: Three representative membrane-distillation configurations; heating, cooling, pumping, and heat recovery
empirical_data_or_code: Publisher states data are in article and supplementary information
source_supported_finding: Reports cooling duty can reach 80–100% of heating in some open-loop configurations; pumping can be material at low single-pass recovery; free heat alone does not guarantee viability.
relevance_to_this_project: Directly constrains the research design: cooling-side availability, pumping, and hydraulic recovery must be modeled alongside recoverable AI heat.
limitation_or_non_claim: Does not by itself quantify AI data-center cooling-water displacement or geographic net freshwater impact.
license_or_reuse_note: Open access is reported by publisher; verify exact license before adapting tables or figures.

citation: Keshavarzzadeh (2020), Design and bio-inspired optimization of direct contact membrane distillation for desalination based on constructal law
study_type: Mechanistic model with reproduced experimental comparison
system_scope: Flat-sheet counter-current DCMD; two flow rates and four NaCl concentrations
empirical_data_or_code: Open-access article; Figure 3 is a secondary-reproduced experimental-marker benchmark
source_supported_finding: Presents a one-dimensional DCMD model and compares flux against experimental markers over feed temperature, flow, and salinity.
relevance_to_this_project: Useful source-equation reconstruction benchmark for the project's membrane-transport layer.
limitation_or_non_claim: The Figure 3 caption's cited reference does not cleanly match the 1999 MD paper in its bibliography; markers must be cross-walked to the primary source. Source-paper agreement is not validation of this repository.
license_or_reuse_note: CC BY 4.0 article license; attribute and mark modifications.

citation: Martínez-Díez and Vázquez-González (1999), Temperature and concentration polarization in membrane distillation of aqueous salt solutions
system_scope: Flat-sheet TF200 PTFE DCMD; water and NaCl solutions; temperature and recirculation-rate variation
empirical_data_or_code: Primary article metadata and abstract verified; numerical observation extraction pending

relevance_to_this_project: Primary provenance target for the 2020 reproduced DCMD benchmark and a candidate unfitted validation dataset.
limitation_or_non_claim: Repository has not yet completed the numerical extraction, exact boundary-condition crosswalk, digitization archive, or independent repeat extraction.

citation: Ali, Orfi, and Najib (2020), Developing and validating a dynamic model of water production by direct-contact membrane distillation
study_type: Dynamic model compared with pilot transient experiments
system_scope: 10 m² spiral-wound counter-current DCMD; stepped hot-feed conditions; 50–300 L/h
empirical_data_or_code: Five publisher-listed XLSX supporting-data files; extraction pending
source_supported_finding: Measured accumulated mass is sampled every 10 s; cold inlet temperature fluctuates and heater steps are not instantaneous. The paper reports substantial uncorrected mismatch and about 3% error only after a tuned heat-loss correction.
relevance_to_this_project: Candidate transient validation source for testing workload/heat intermittency and model response lag.
limitation_or_non_claim: The published tuned result is not independent validation; exact input histories and raw/processed-data distinctions must be reconstructed before model comparison.
license_or_reuse_note: CC BY 4.0 per publisher; attribute source and document modifications.

citation: Sulaiman et al. (2026), Sustainable water recovery from steel industry wastewater via direct contact membrane distillation
empirical_data_or_code: Open-access early version with supplementary material; quantitative extraction pending
source_supported_finding: Abstract reports flux 1.4–4.8 kg m⁻² h⁻¹, salt rejection above 99.9%, and stable operation up to 93% recovery; model is compared with 14 literature datasets.
relevance_to_this_project: Recent adjacent work on industrial water and heat reuse; useful to test transferability limits and sharpen the research gap.
limitation_or_non_claim: Different feed chemistry and hollow-fiber geometry; its reported performance cannot be transferred directly to AI-data-center heat or freshwater accounting.
license_or_reuse_note: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; do not redistribute adapted tables/figures; extract facts with attribution and verify reuse conditions.

citation: Hu et al. (2025), Heat-mass transfer and energy efficiency in direct contact membrane distillation: Effects of membrane properties, temperature, and salt concentration
system_scope: DCMD with PTFE/PVDF membranes and high-salinity wastewater
empirical_data_or_code: Publisher abstract and article metadata verified; full-text access restricted in current retrieval

relevance_to_this_project: Requires the study to treat membrane-property, temperature-polarization, concentration-polarization, and scaling uncertainty as coupled constraints rather than assuming constant flux.
